Let's say that a person's business email and URL both end with the same domain. Do you think it's reasonable to avoid redundancy by omitting your URL from your business cards?

Example: (an email address of) info@business.com (and directly below that) business.com

In 2015 it seems like this shouldn't cause undue confusion as the URL is available. What do you think? Go for the safe, redundant option, or challenge the norms and allow people to use their brains a little?
Avoiding redundancy by leaving URL off business cards.
Depends on your industry, anything tech related I'm sure that's fine, but never underestimate peoples stupidity.

You would be surprised how many non-internet savvy people are in the business world. The fact that the two domains are the same does not mean they will equate the connection, or the fact that they go to the sameish place.

My business email and company domain are the same (.net in both cases) and I have people forward me emails they tried to send to me earlier in the week, only to see ".com" in the address bar of the forwarded message.

In business, it's better to lay it all out than to try to be streamlined, unless your industry is sufficiently versed in the internet.
I'd err on the side of clarity and put them both on there.

Most of my clients are old people who would rather call/fax than email...We do have a website but it's primarily for people who search for us (not people who already have our business card). I use the back to put a simplistic map on it, though. Or pricing coupons (so the business card doubles as a coupon). Double sided business cards woohoo!
